ALLEGATION_VERDICT: REAL_FATAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/ex-the-alexander-subbase-lemma-applied-to-a-closed-interval.md:66, used at step 4.1
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: “[L4] The order of ℝ is total, and 0 ≤ t ≤ 1 for every t ∈ L.”
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: items/def-real-order.md says, “Independence of the representative, trichotomy, and compatibility with the field operations: [[thm-reals-ordered-field]].” The omitted theorem states, “The relation of [[def-real-order]] is well defined and makes ℝ ([[thm-reals-field]]) a totally ordered field.”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: Neither cited target directly establishes that the relation defined as the real order is total. The real-order definition explicitly delegates trichotomy to thm-reals-ordered-field. Def-interval calls the reals a complete ordered field but does not establish that the specific constructed relation satisfies the ordered-field axioms. Step 4.1 requires totality for its dichotomy. Under the binding citation-fidelity rule, this missing theorem citation is fatal even though the underlying order fact is standard.

OTHER_FINDINGS:
LOCATION: items/ex-the-alexander-subbase-lemma-applied-to-a-closed-interval.md:64 and step 2.1 at line 76
QUOTE: “[L3] Every nonempty subset of ℝ bounded above has a least upper bound” and “so [L3] gives s := sup C”
DEFECT: L3 cites definitions and the epsilon characterization but no result establishing that the constructed real numbers possess the least-upper-bound property. Step 2.1 depends on the existence of the supremum, not merely on its definition.
EVIDENCE: items/def-complete-ordered-field.md only defines the condition: “F is a complete ordered field … if every nonempty S subset of F that is bounded above has a least upper bound in F.” The result that actually establishes the needed property is items/cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete.md: “The Cauchy-sequence reals have the least-upper-bound property: every nonempty S subset of the Cauchy-sequence reals that is bounded above has a least upper bound.”
